text: Not to beat about the bush (for the advantages of the scheme would take a week to tell) what’s to prevent your marrying her?’ Richard Swiveller, who had been looking over the rim of the tumbler while his companion addressed the foregoing remarks to him with great energy and earnestness of manner, no sooner heard these words than he evinced the utmost consternation, and with difficulty ejaculated the monosyllable: ‘What!’ ‘I say, what’s to prevent,’ repeated the other with a steadiness of manner, of the effect of which upon his companion he was well assured by long experience, ‘what’s to prevent your marrying her?’ ‘And she “nearly fourteen”!’ cried Dick. ‘I don’t mean marrying her now’--returned the brother angrily; ‘say in two year’s time, in three, in four. Does the old man look like a long-liver?’ ‘He don’t look like it,’ said Dick shaking his head, ‘but these old people--there’s no trusting them, Fred. There’s an aunt of mine down in Dorsetshire that was going to die when I was eight years old, and hasn’t kept her word yet.
